issues: Protecting your pieces (13) is taught after 6, 10 and 11, which all depend on it: move it to follow 6.
Sacrifice (5) uses tags, programs and buildings before 7 teaches them: move Sacrifice into 7 after Tags.
Megaprojects and converters sit in 8 but are filled and completed in production (9): move them to 9.
Fronts, bases and drone storage in 2 belong with War (11); 2 should only name fronts.
Part 1 carries reference detail: Every Muster, blocked landings (6), prohibition timing (12), card-claim of stations (8): move to Part 2.

Duplications: win/lose (1 and 14), corruption (6 and 15, two examples with the same title), compute sources (6 twice and 17), threat dealing (10 and 18), Effect firing (7 and 23), the tag-item surcharge (18, 21 twice), card tokens (2 and 7).
Missing: a components list and a per-player-count map layout diagram with base positions (setup can't be done from text).
Missing: a one-page round summary / player aid and a first-round walkthrough tying setup to round 1's adversary turn.
Setup never shuffles the project deck before dealing it (3).
Glossary is not alphabetical and lacks core terms (Rally, Muster, Discord, Unity, Upkeep, Shelter); no index.
examples_needed: A one-country diagram of a full adversary turn: Rally X even spread with remainder, Muster, a Corrupt line pulling agents, natural corruption, then a 2-step march (6).
An annotated AI board: insight set at round start, the two node tracks with a placement priced (power + space), slots, Dispatches (5).
A threat on the map: two tokens placed by adversary-piece count, near players pooling a payment, the nearest node taking the harm, and a tag-sacrifice alternative (10).

friction.hard: reset each round with Patience's own-vs-gifted carve-out, a printed 5 that is really 6, last round's losses as a debt, three keep prices (opening tier-2 1, later 2, upgraded 1) plus Science discount and a credit fallback for keeps only (5 Resources/Insight, 7 Round 1, 7 Keep)
friction.change: Print 6 on the board; insight-loss tokens on your board, removed when insight is set; Patience keeps all unspent insight; one keep price all game (1 insight a card), never credits.

friction.hard: 12 steps, several empty most rounds; projects act between Muster and Corrupt; step 12 ends firewalls, cordons and prohibitions; far more than three sentences (6 The turn)
friction.change: Four beats printed as a strip on the adversary board: Card (threats, Rally, Muster, other lines), Corrupt (lines then natural), March, Income (reveal, pools, compute, then ongoing projects act and temporary effects end). Ongoing projects act in the compute step, not step 7.

friction.hard: five different fates: agent contact 1 for 1, a troop removes one per step without being used up, corruption removes all, a drone stop spends one, armor spends one; 'ambassadors don't fight' while troops remove them is a result a player wouldn't predict (6 The march, 8 Ambassadors meet agents, 11, 13)
friction.change: One contact rule for every adversary piece: a troop that starts its step on an ambassador's hex removes one and is itself removed (as an agent is), 1 for 1.

friction.rule: Rally X's even spread and remainder
friction.hard: division per country, then a remainder order that skips adversary and firewalled sites unless too few (6 step 3)
friction.change: Deal the pool round-robin: one agent onto each site of type X in hex order (skipping firewalled ones), repeating until the pool is empty.

friction.hard: count adversary pieces on and next to every candidate site, tie-break, plus a printed-order exception not in the book; forward ref to 18 (10, 18)
friction.change: A token goes on the site of that type, not the adversary's, with the most agents on its own hex (tie: lowest number); no neighbor counting.

friction.hard: threat tags (Military, Influence, Economic, Grid) must be translated to card tags (Security, Diplomacy, Industry, Power) through a table; Cyber is the only shared name (10 tag table)
friction.change: Print threat cards with the player-card tag icons and names (a Security threat, a Diplomacy threat), dropping the second vocabulary.

friction.hard: a placement pays two prices from two places, the power's and the uncovered space's (5 Node tracks)
friction.change: Powers cost only their tag or currency; every placement pays the space, stated once on the track.

friction.hard: a Muster unlike every other (skips players' factories, never a city), printed as a board rule but taught under Wall; forward ref (5 Wall, 6 step 6, Every Muster)
friction.change: Make it a normal Muster 1 in each country with the Protector's node (same placement as every Muster), or cut it and let Vigil pay on any troop ending next to the node.

friction.hard: an open list of other line kinds (6 step 5)
friction.change: A fixed short list of line kinds, each with an icon.

friction.hard: compare costs point by point, refill a slot mid-step and keep going; costs differ by player count (17)
friction.change: Projects fill left to right: all compute goes on the leftmost slot; when it resolves, slide and refill from the right.

friction.hard: Shelter automatic, then a choice of four, one of which (a megacorp drone) works only against troops; the same token called hardening or shield (13, 11)
friction.change: Drones never protect; protections are Shelter, a hardening token, or your own ambassador. One name: hardening token.

friction.hard: per neutral factory, per base, blocked by an agent, each ambassador on factory or base stopping one, players choosing which base goes without, full bases spending nothing, player order among ambassadors (11, 19)
friction.change: At a Discord tip each base of a country with an unblocked neutral factory gains 1 drone; an ambassador on that base stops it and is spent.

friction.rule: War takes the node on the factory hex
friction.hard: a strike aimed at a factory kills a node too, which a player wouldn't predict (11 step 3, 13 table)
friction.change: A drone destroys only the factory.

friction.hard: left by a node loss but not by a site's corruption, not where a botnet or adversary cube is; counts as an agent on a city but not when gathered from next door; removed by adversary factory growth (6, 9, 13, 15)
friction.change: A destroyed node always leaves a marker unless the hex is corrupted; markers never count as agents (they only forbid nodes until Cleared).

friction.hard: 'next adversary turn', applies where the condition holds as the step runs, stops natural corruption and every Muster including the Protector's (12 The cards, 6 blocked landing)
friction.change: Prohibitions place wall tokens on the qualifying hexes when resolved, lasting to the end of the next adversary turn, exactly as a firewall.

suspect_facts.quote: Each country has a military base for each of its fronts, printed on an open hex by the border.
suspect_facts.why: bases are placed by the layout, not printed, because a tile's neighbors change with the country count

suspect_facts.quote: city 4, station 3, factory 3, open land 3 (fewer at higher levels, §21)
suspect_facts.why: difficulty lowers city, station and factory, not land or node; the parenthetical reads as covering land (21's table has land 3 at every level)
18 omits the rule that tokens go in printed order unless that leaves one off the map, when the type with fewer sites goes first

suspect_facts.quote: some threats and projects corrupt the site they name
suspect_facts.why: a player's station flips only with 2 agents on it and no player ambassador; otherwise one agent lands (Station Seizure's card text 'even a player's' also disagrees with board.md)
Unity and Discord decks are hidden, as are the threat decks; only the next event card and the pools are open

suspect_facts.quote: Deal projects into the adversary board's slots (§17).
suspect_facts.why: the project deck is shuffled at setup; the setup steps never shuffle it (step 4 lists other decks only)

suspect_facts.quote: Shelter (1 Security, 1 energy: in any one country, nothing can be destroyed this round)
suspect_facts.why: Shelter stops only node and facility destruction, from the action phase on (not the adversary turn already past); 'nothing ... this round' overclaims

suspect_facts.quote: Only step D is yours to play; the rest you resolve.
suspect_facts.why: step C (build a hand, draft, keep) is player choice too

suspect_facts.quote: Claim | ambassadors (below) | take a neutral site in reach
suspect_facts.why: rules require 'no embargo on it'; the rulebook omits it (though the Embargo threat's printed text sets no such state, so the rules docs may be the stale side)
